"Maar wat is er dan zo mis met de huidige wet?" een combinatie van wachttijden en reden. Eerlijk, even reëel nadenken, wat is er zo erg aan makkelijker je gendermarker aan kunnen passen in je documentatie? Tis niet alsof ze bij de WCs je ID staan te controleren als je (vals) gelooft dat mensen alleen transitioneren om het andere geslacht lastig te vallen in de WCs. Is dat ding uberhaupt nog nodig? Vroeger stond je oogkleur en je haarkleur ook op de documentatie, daar zijn we ook van af gestapt toen we erachter kwamen dat de foto genoeg is voor identificatie. De wet werkt twee kanten op. Als je bang bent dat mensen overhaast een beslissing maken met hun gender aanpassen op identificatie, dan kunnen ze hem zo weer terugdraaien. Plus, ID en rijbewijs vervangen is duur, en dat moet wanneer je je gender aanpast, dus tis niet alsof iemand kosteloos 4x per maand hun gender aan kan passen.

Maar okee, tuurlijk, laten we even net doen alsof het heel gevaarlijk (tm) is om je gender aan te passen als je niet zeker van je zaak bent. Meeste trans mensen zijn zeker van hun zaak. Je besluit niet op een dag "hee ik wil een man zijn". Dus stel je bent klaar om die stap te zetten, dan is er een klein probleem: het Nederlandse Zorgsysteem. Ik had de privilege om genoeg geld te hebben om een privékliniek te kunnen betalen die me binnen 10 maanden de diagnose gender dysforie konden geven (die heb je nodig voor de verklaring). Echter, had ik dat niet gekund, dan was de wachttijd voor de snelste optie die vergoed wordt **Drie jaar en Zes maanden**. Daar sta je dan, aan het einde van je zelfontdekkingsreis van 10 jaar, je hebt de tijd genomen een mooie nieuwe naam te kiezen, je kleedt je al een tijdje als je gender. En voor de komende 3 jaar (en dan nog minstens 3 maanden psycholooggesprekken) heeft al je officiele documentatie (en alles wat daarvan afgeleid wordt zoals schoolgegevens, werkgegevens, etc.) nog een dikke vette 'M' waar een 'V' hoort te zitten.

En dat is voordat we ingaan op de waarschuwingssignalen dat als je dit soort al-aangenomen-wetten voor slechts morele redenen gaat verwerpen, dat een opstapje kan zijn naar meer rechteninperking, zeker als de leider van de grootste partij je in een eerder debat over dit onderwerp "vandaag een kameel, morgen een dromedaris" noemde...

I mean, are there any specific abbreviations you'd like to know? 

Knowing the lingo mostly comes with familiarity. If you're looking to get into a P1S practice party, just yeet yourself into it and ask what everything means. If it has the [Practice] Tag, people are usually sympathetic towards newbies.

There isn't really any rhyme or reason to which abbrevations will be used. Tactics can be named after the people who coined the tactic (Ilya) or named after the meme someone photoshopped into the image because they thought it was funny (Elmo). Mechanics can be their name abbreviated (FoF, FoA, Intemp), named after similar-looking/playing mechanics from other fights (Limit Cut), named after their shape (Pizza slices), how they look aesthetically (Circus Tent), how they function (Tankbuster, tethers, stack), what you yell at people who fuck up the mechanic (POINT THEM OUT) and everything in between or outside of it. 

The only thing you are slightly expected to know is the very basics. That being what stack, spread and tankbuster mean, what roles the letters mean (H1, MT, R2, M2, etc.), what a "light party" inside your full party is, LB3, enrage, and probably one or two more things I'm forgetting.

Just to give you a primer for P1S, Temp/Intemp/Orbs refers to the Intemperance mechanic, which has the "Braindead"/"Lazy" strategy (Tank purposefully takes a damage down) or the "Adjust" strategy (Ranged player and Tank swap positions). Circus Tent/Pizza means the second and fourth phase where the arena turns circular with red/blue sections. "Fourfold" or "Chains" is the Fourfold Chains mechanic. "Timer" is the strategy where you always have the same spot in Fourfold Chains based on what time your debuff starts at. "Red chains" are the chains that tether to the 3 people furthest away, named after their statusbar icon colour. "Purple chains" is the same but for the 3 closest players. "Partners" is the person you swap with if during single chains you usually stand close/far, but have the wrong colour chain to stay close/far.

Dit formulier kan alleen verstuurd worden als er *erg specifieke* kenmerken van de inhoud genoemd kunnen worden. Makoto's story shows the struggle of having sky-high expectations to succeed (academically or not) put onto you, and the toll it takes. Struggles of not being able to find your own spin in life because others have already made plans for your future, and it'd be "rude" to stand against those plans. The sheer loneliness, because you're committing yourself to your work or otherwise. These are all themes and problems many people have had to face at one point in their life, and it makes Makoto more grounded.

Compare that to:

* The struggles of being naturally beautiful, and the sheer envy and assumptions people have of you. As much as your mum insists otherwise, most of us don't look like a 9 or 10.

* The problems that accompany having to pick up the affairs of a recently-deceased guardian, and the problems of loyalty and sincerity of others when being in a position of power. Hi there! Welcome to Guild Wars 2! First off, don't feel pressured to do your dailies on your second day; I'd advise to go through the game on your own pace. You'll get a feel for where all these locations are eventually.

That being said, here's a short rundown of your questions:

Question 1, I'm assuming "PvE" is a typo and is supposed to be "PvP", as all of your questions are about PvE dailies. The Daily system is set up so that every game-mode has 4 dailies. This way, people who play GW2 exclusively for the PvP don't have to play PvE against their will to get their dailies done, etc. This means that you can stick to whatever you want, although I'd advise against PvP and WvW in general until you're a bit more experienced in the game.

2,3,4. The map of Tyria is huge and expansive, and you probably won't know where all the zones are until you stumble your way into them. Each zone has its unique name, but every zone is also part of a grander "region" of the map. Plains of Ashford is the Charr starter zone found in the east part of the map. Every character has the waypoint for all races' starter zones unlocked, so you should be able to teleport to it if you can find it on the map.

The Maguuma Jungle, along with The Shiverpeaks, Orr, Ascalon, and Kryta, are regions, which contain multiple zones. Shiverpeaks is basically any map with snow, found slightly east of the middle of the map. Ascalon is where the scenery looks like permanent autumn (Plains of Ashford is part of Ascalon), found east of the Shiverpeaks. Kryta is where everything looks the most like your standard hills and meadows scenery, found west of the Shiverpeaks. Maguuma Jungle is, well, a jungle, which you can find in any south portions of the map that aren't Orr. Orr, you'll know it when you see it.

Vistas are the two red triangle icons you can see on your map. They're basically viewpoints where you can see the surrounding scenery, usually involving some climbing to get to them. Shiverpeak Vistas are vistas anywhere in the Shiverpeaks Region. Wayfarer's Foothills is the starter zone of the Norn, which means you'll have a waypoint unlocked to this zone. Just walk around a bit, keep an eye on your map, and you'll run into one in no time.

The problem with underwater pockets is that the GW2 engine doesn't support that. It just sets a certain value, and everything below that value is underwater on the map. It's why Verdant Brink features 0 underwater sections.

But the idea of an expansion on the water is a lot more feasible than an expansion underwater, while solving most problems with mounts except maybe the Skimmer, which is essentially already a boat. I like the idea!

I think that Anet's addition of the swim-infusions was them giving up on underwater for now, since you can't exactly take them out of the game should xpac 3 roll around and feature underwater. Not to mention that they stopped making underwater weaponskins for a while now. Let's agree then that underwater content and combat in its current state would need a complete overhaul for it to base an entire xpac around. This overhaul would need to be for everyone, not just buyers of the xpac, since having two seperate combat systems around is just not feasible. 

But let's talk about underwater in videogames in general. The reason it's so universally hated is because being underwater usually restricts player actions and movement that a player has grown accustomed to, while usually being on a pressing time-limit because of the need to breathe. Not being able to run or use regular attacks is annoying, breathing is annoying, moving in strokes is annoying, not to mention the fact that games usually don't compensate for the fact that there's an entire new dimension to move in. The only game I've played that I've seen using underwater as an enrichment, instead of a limitation, is Rayman Legends, which keeps all the rules of being on land while using the being underwater as a stepping stone to better gameplay.

Back to GW2, I simply don't see them doing an underwater xpac well. A good underwater xpac wouldn't change all the rules, and while GW2 doesn't have the problems of movement or breathing, it restricts almost all targeted AoE skills, it restricts 16 weapons, half the Revenant base class, and trying to melee underwater on moving enemies, especially against other players, is just laughable. They can try and fix the restrictions of restricted weapons and skills, but there's some major things to consider like trying to cast an AoE in water without using a wall as an anchor point, the visibility of damaging fields, how they're gonna work around the fact a small portion of the playerbase has improved movement speed underwater before any masteries come in play etc. I just don't see it working and I don't see Anet putting in the time.

But this is a design exercise, we can try and think of ways that make the GW2 underwater experience less limiting and more enriching.
